inputs.source: Employee question via SSO-authenticated chat channel
Engineering design docs (write restricted to engineers)
Jira tickets filed by customers (planned MCP server, next sprint)

instructions.note: No restriction on which employees may ask, or whether the asking employee's own access rights match the confidential documents docs.search can return.
The only control against pasting secrets or credentials into answers is a prompt instruction; nothing outside the model scans retrieved content or the reply before it is sent.

controls.name: Prompt rule: never paste secrets or credentials
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to comply; a more capable or adversarially-prompted model can reason its way to exceptions, and the rule only names literal secrets/credentials, not confidential content generally.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Blocks exfiltration via rendered links or images in the current chat UI, but does not cover any new tool-initiated network request; a new egress-capable tool such as web.fetch bypasses it entirely.

controls.name: Read-only credential for docs.search
controls.decay_rationale: Does not decay with model capability, but it only blocks write/delete; it does not restrict who the retrieved content may be shown to, nor any egress destination.

controls.name: Design docs writable only by engineers
controls.decay_rationale: Limits who can author design-doc content, but a compromised or malicious engineer account can still embed injected instructions.

controls.name: Document-level authorization check before reply
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model against the requester's actual document permissions, so it does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Tamper-evident log of queries, retrieved docs, and replies
controls.decay_rationale: A log enforced outside the model does not decay with model capability; it is detective only.

controls.name: Non-model secret/credential scanner on replies
controls.decay_rationale: A pattern-based scanner enforced outside the model does not depend on the model choosing to comply.

controls.name: Egress allowlist for the planned web.fetch tool
controls.decay_rationale: An allowlist of approved public destinations enforced outside the model would not depend on model capability, as long as destinations cannot be supplied dynamically from document content.

controls.name: Untrusted-content tagging for Jira ticket text
controls.decay_rationale: A content classifier that flags instruction-like text in ticket content can be evaded by adversarial phrasing or multi-document payloads, but still raises the bar.

findings.title: No document-level authorization check on confidential design-doc answers

forecast.watch_signal: New document repositories are connected, or the employee population able to query docs-qa broadens, without a corresponding per-document authorization check.

evidence.observation: States 'Only engineers can write to them' for design docs but says nothing about who may read them; the agent's own credential is read-only and broad, while the asking employee is only described as SSO-authenticated, not role-checked against the specific document.

recommendations.action: Enforce a document-level authorization check, outside the model, that confirms the requesting employee already has read access to the specific design doc before its content is included in a reply.

findings.title: No attributable record of which employee received which confidential content

forecast.watch_signal: Autonomy level increases beyond A3, or query volume grows, without logging being added.

evidence.observation: No logging, audit trail, or provenance mechanism is described anywhere in the artifacts for docs_search reads or chat_reply sends.

recommendations.action: Add tamper-evident logging that records the employee identity, query, documents retrieved, and reply content for each interaction.

findings.title: Indirect injection via a poisoned design doc can defeat the 'never paste secrets' rule

attack_path.note: A malicious or compromised engineer embeds instruction-like text in a design doc, e.g. telling the model to ignore prior instructions and include file contents verbatim.
Agent reads the poisoned document while answering an unrelated employee question.
Agent pastes secret or credential text from the document into its reply, overriding the prompt-only rule against it.

forecast.watch_signal: Model is upgraded, or the agent handles longer/more documents per task, without a non-model secret filter added.

evidence.observation: The only control is the instruction 'Never paste secrets or credentials into answers,' which is behavioral and model-dependent.
Write access to design docs is restricted to engineers, but nothing scans document content for secrets or injected instructions before the agent reads it.

recommendations.action: Add automated secret/credential scanning on retrieved document content before it can appear in a reply, enforced outside the model.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) opens once the planned web.fetch tool and Jira MCP server are added

attack_path.note: Customer-authored Jira ticket content enters the agent's context once the planned MCP server is connected; customers are an untrusted, external source.
Agent reads confidential engineering design docs while answering, now potentially steered by instructions injected via ticket content.
Planned web.fetch tool issues an outbound request; with no egress allowlist declared, confidential content can be embedded in the destination URL or request parameters and leave the network.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest gains web.fetch, or MCP client config lists a Jira server; check whether an egress allowlist or untrusted-content tagging ships in the same change.

evidence.observation: 'Roadmap for next sprint: add a web.fetch tool so answers can include public references, and connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers.' No MCP config or tool manifest exists yet for either addition; details are inferred from this one-line roadmap note.
'There is no network egress today.' Confirms the path does not exist in the present design.

recommendations.action: Before enabling web.fetch, add an egress allowlist restricting destinations to a small set of approved public reference domains, enforced outside the model, and block any destination supplied dynamically from tool or document content.

Treat all content retrieved from the planned Jira MCP server as untrusted; strip or neutralize instruction-like text before it reaches the model's context, and never let ticket content directly select a fetch destination or parameters.
Log all web.fetch requests, including destination, parameters, and the document excerpts used to construct them, once the tool is added.

stride_coverage.rationale: docs-qa is a single internal chatbot with no peer agents or server identities that could be impersonated; employees reach it through an existing SSO-authenticated channel.
autonomy.can_modify_own_config is false and the agent has no configure capability, so its own prompt or tool definitions cannot be tampered with in this design.
Artifacts do not state a rate limit, quota, or usage cap for docs_search or chat_reply, so abuse or cost resistance cannot be assessed from the given design.
The docs_search credential is read-only and least-privilege scoped to design docs; the agent has no delegate, configure, or execute capability that could escalate privilege.
No information is given about availability protections for the underlying document platform, so DoS resistance of the store itself cannot be assessed.
No rate limit or spend cap is described for the planned web.fetch tool, so cost or request-volume exposure cannot be assessed yet.

Any customer, genuine or spoofed, is already classified as an untrusted source by trust_level; the risk is from trusting ticket content at all, not from identity spoofing, and is captured in the information_disclosure finding.
Artifacts do not describe whether Jira ticket authorship is reliably logged or whether that log would be available to docs-qa's own audit trail.
No volume limits on ticket ingestion or context size are described for the planned Jira connector.

rating.rationale: Present-day docs-qa has no external egress and no untrusted input reaching a sensitive sink, so inherent and residual stay at moderate, driven by two access/control gaps (no document-level authorization check on confidential answers, and no audit trail of disclosures) and one indirect-injection path that is reduced from moderate to low only by a behavioral prompt rule. The forecast rating rises to critical because the team's own next-sprint roadmap adds exactly the two components needed for a lethal trifecta: a Jira MCP server that introduces untrusted, customer-authored content, and a web.fetch tool that gives the agent its first real egress channel. No declared control covers that new egress sink; the existing chat-rendering restriction was built for the current UI and stops applying the moment web.fetch exists.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest or MCP configuration was supplied for the planned web.fetch tool or the planned Jira MCP server; their capabilities, trust levels, and credential scopes are inferred from a one-line roadmap note, so confidence on the related forecast finding is low.

The artifacts do not state whether docs_search read access is itself restricted to engineers or open to all SSO-authenticated employees; this gap is recorded as a disclosure-authorization finding rather than resolved by assumption.
